chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:
I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say:

Concerning a woman who gifted her slave-girl to her husband, and he had intercourse with her, and the slave-girl became pregnant: then the woman became jealous and denied that she had gifted her to him, and said, ‘She is my slave-girl.’ Then when she feared that he would be stoned, she admitted that she had in fact gifted her to him. So when she admitted the gift, he administered to her the hadd punishment.

key_terms.أَقَرَّتْ: She confessed or acknowledged, admitting the truth of the gift.
key_terms.أَنْكَرَتْ: She denied, meaning she repudiated the prior gift.
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: The prescribed hadd punishment applied in this case.
key_terms.الْهِبَةِ: The gift, referring to the transfer of the slave-girl to the husband.
key_terms.جَارِيَتَهَا: Her slave-girl, the female bondswoman at the center of the legal case.
key_terms.فَغَارَتِ: She became jealous, describing the motive behind her later denial.
key_terms.فَوَقَعَ عَلَيْهَا: He had intercourse with her, indicating marital-type lawful access based on ownership transfer.
key_terms.وَهَبَتْ: She gave as a gift, transferring ownership without compensation.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman falsely denies gifting her slave-girl to her husband and causes an accusation of illicit intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a legal case involving a wife who gifted her slave-girl to her husband, then later denied the gift out of jealousy after the slave-girl became pregnant. When she finally confessed the truth after fearing that her husband would be subjected to rajm, Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام stated that she was given the hadd punishment for her false accusation.
